featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely shocked and extremely disappointed with the customer service at Aza Juhu today.
Was buying the product of : lehenga by Rimple and Harpreet

As a pregnant woman, I visited the store with my mom to buy a lehenga for her. We selected a piece from the sale section and before billing, we clearly spoke with the in-store tailor regarding alterations and measurements. He answered our questions and gave us the impression that alterations could be managed.

In fact, the store staff themselves confirmed that the tailor would be available (screenshot attached). Based on that confirmation, we proceeded further.

However, once we finalized the lehenga, the tailor suddenly backed off and refused to take measurements, saying he cannot travel to Malad and that taking measurements outside the store is “not allowed.” This was never clearly communicated earlier when we had the discussion before billing.

I politely explained my situation and requested if they could please make an exception considering I am pregnant. We were even ready to pay any additional charges the tailor demanded. Despite this, the tailor simply refused, and the staff member Manjari along with her manager were extremely rude and dismissive, repeatedly hiding behind “store rules” instead of trying to help or find a solution.

For a premium brand like Aza, the complete lack of empathy, transparency, and basic customer service was shocking. The screenshot of the chat clearly shows the store confirming the tailor’s availability, yet the experience at the store was the exact opposite.

This experience has been deeply frustrating and unacceptable, and after today, I can confidently say I will never shop from Aza again.

I hope the management at Aza Juhu seriously reviews how their staff treat customers—because respect, honesty, and empathy should be the minimum standard.

featured_reviews.name: Priyank Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Natraj Market – Honest Shopping Review

There’s a lot of buzz around The Natraj Market when it comes to ethnic shopping, so I finally decided to visit it to buy a lehenga for my own roka.

I’ll break this down into key aspects—location, layout, shops, collection, pricing, discounts, and overall value.

⸻

📍 Location

Natraj Market is located right outside Malad Railway Station (West) and is barely a 5-minute walk, making it extremely convenient in terms of accessibility.

⸻

🛍️ Market Layout & Shops

The moment you enter the market and walk down a few steps, it feels like a maze—multiple narrow lanes and countless turns that can easily leave you disoriented.
The entire market is dedicated to women’s ethnic wear, with shop after shop selling similar categories.

I personally visited around 10 stores, including Devi, Resham, Mukht, Purple, Sangam, and a few others.

⸻

👗 Collection

The collection, in my opinion, was decent but nothing exceptional. The variety felt limited, mainly because most shops stock only a few pieces per design.
If you’re looking for something very specific, it becomes slightly difficult. Personally, I wasn’t very satisfied and often felt that my time was being wasted due to the lack of standout options.

⸻

💰 Pricing

Price points generally start at around ₹8,000 and go up to ₹20,000. However, considering the collection, the pricing felt on the higher side.

⸻

🏷️ Discounts & Bargaining

An interesting observation—just when you start walking out of a store, the shopkeeper suddenly offers an instant 30–40% discount, often adding that the price is still negotiable.
This becomes even more evident when you realise that similar designs are available in Dadar Market for less than half the price.

⸻

⚖️ Convenience Cost

What you’re essentially paying for here is convenience—location, accessibility, and everything under one roof. The premium doesn’t always justify the product.

⸻

✅ Final Verdict

Natraj Market works if you’re short on time and want quick access to ethnic wear near the station. However, if you’re looking for better variety, value for money, and unique designs, exploring markets like Dadar might be a wiser choice.
